name: devkit-for-strapi-mcp

tools.name: server_info
tools.description: Identify the running DevKit server: its version, whether a Pro licence is active, how many tools are genuinely callable, the roots being indexed, and how current the index is (`freshness`). `tools/list` advertises the Pro tools too, but without a licence they return an upsell instead of running — this reports which ones will really work, so an agent stops guessing. Also the only way to name a version in a bug report: the version lives in the MCP handshake, which the client consumes and does not always display.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List the Strapi projects discovered in the workspace (name, root, Strapi version, counts, `freshness`). Call this first in a multi-project workspace, then pass `from`/`project` to the other tools; project_info gives one project in full.

tools.name: project_info
tools.description: Everything about one project before acting on it: Strapi version (installed / declared), TypeScript or JavaScript, package manager, API prefix, counts (APIs, content-types by kind, components, services, controllers, policies, middlewares, routes), every local and installed plugin with whether DevKit verifies refs into it and, if not, why (no node_modules, rewritten at boot by a project file, a src/extensions override, Enterprise-only code…), health (broken refs, refs into unverified plugins) and freshness. Call it to orient yourself in an unknown project, or when a plugin ref comes back `external`.

from.description: A path inside the target project (e.g. the file you are editing). Disambiguates a multi-project workspace.

project.description: A project name (its folder) or root path. Use when you have no file path in hand.

tools.name: add_project
tools.description: Locate and index a Strapi project on demand from an ABSOLUTE path — either the project root, or any file/folder inside it (the server walks up to the project root; a folder is also scanned downward for monorepos). Use this when a tool returns `noProject`. Idempotent. Returns the projects now known (use a name/root with `from`/`project`).

path.description: Absolute path to the Strapi project root, or to any file/folder inside it.

tools.name: refresh
tools.description: Re-scan every discovered Strapi project from disk and rebuild the index from scratch. Rarely needed: before every call the server already compares the project files with the disk and re-indexes what was created, edited or deleted outside this session (manual edits, git checkout/pull, another tool), and re-reads installed plugins after an install. Use it to discover a project added since startup, after external edits on a project whose `freshness.diskTracking` is 'off' (too many files), or with `cold: true` to also drop the cached plugin reads and read every installed plugin from node_modules again (slower). Returns the projects with their `freshness`.

cold.description: Also drop the cached plugin reads: every installed plugin is read again from node_modules (default false).

Read from the schemas, not from a running Strapi. Paste it in a README, a doc or an issue; `focus` narrows it to some types and their neighbours. With `strapiFields`, adds what Strapi gives every content-type (createdAt, updatedAt, publishedAt, createdBy/updatedBy → admin::user).

tools.name: list_routes
tools.description: List a project's HTTP route table: method, path, mounted `fullPath` (API prefix included), handler, policies, middlewares, `public` (auth: false), `auth` when customized, and where each route is declared (`filePath`/`offset`). Covers the project's explicit routes, the auto-CRUD routes synthesized from createCoreRouter, and the routes local and installed plugins declare (`origin`), read from node_modules without booting Strapi. Admin-panel routes are left out unless `admin: true`. Filter with `method`, `path` (a pattern, a part of it, or a concrete URL such as `/api/articles/12`) and `handler`. With `pipeline: true` (needs a filter, at most 20 routes), each route also gets what a request goes through, in Strapi's order — the `config/middlewares` stack (once, in `globalMiddlewares`), auth, policies, route middlewares, handler — each step with a status: `ok`, `not-found-by-strapi` (it exists under another name Strapi won't try: Strapi throws at startup), `unknown`, `unverified`, `unread` or `inline`. Use it to explain a 401/403, or a startup error about a policy or middleware.

handler.description: Only routes whose handler (qualified, e.g. `api::article.article.find`) contains this.

pipeline.description: Add each route's pipeline (needs method, path or handler; at most 20 routes).

What the database holds is not known here.

tools.name: config_sync_diff
tools.description: The diff config-sync's admin page shows, from the real plugin: each entry that differs between config/sync and the database — `different`, `only-in-db`, `only-in-sync-dir` — with what differs in a few words. It includes what a start of Strapi changes on its own (a new field in a content-manager view, the super-admin's permissions…): after changing a schema, a controller or a route, these are the entries to export and commit with the code. With `key`, one entry: every difference, and both sides in full when they fit in one answer. It runs the project's code: Strapi is loaded the way config-sync's own CLI does (no server, no port, no admin account), and a load does what a start of `strapi develop` does to the database (schema sync, pending migrations) — so only on a local development database: a remote one, a Strapi 4 database under Strapi 5 code, or a missing SQLite file are refused before Strapi's bootstrap (where it writes to the database). Takes a few seconds.

key.description: One entry, `<type>.<name>`: every difference, and both sides when they fit.

type.description: Only the entries of one type (`admin-role`, `user-role`, `core-store`, `plugin_content_manager_configuration`…).

tools.description: Write entries from the database into config/sync with the plugin's own export — the exact form config-sync compares, so the files stop showing as different. Only entries that differ are exported; `keys` narrows it (default: every difference). An entry only in config/sync has its file deleted. Commit the files with the code that caused them. It runs the project's code: Strapi is loaded the way config-sync's own CLI does (no server, no port, no admin account), and a load does what a start of `strapi develop` does to the database (schema sync, pending migrations) — so only on a local development database: a remote one, a Strapi 4 database under Strapi 5 code, or a missing SQLite file are refused before Strapi's bootstrap (where it writes to the database).

tools.name: config_sync_import
tools.description: Apply entries of config/sync to the database with the plugin's own import — a role's permissions, a content-manager view, a setting. `keys` is required: never everything at once. An entry only in the database is deleted from it. Afterwards, the entries still different are exported back (`reexport`, default true): the database's own form of what was just imported (a generated documentId…), so the diff converges. Refused with NODE_ENV=production. It runs the project's code: Strapi is loaded the way config-sync's own CLI does (no server, no port, no admin account), and a load does what a start of `strapi develop` does to the database (schema sync, pending migrations) — so only on a local development database: a remote one, a Strapi 4 database under Strapi 5 code, or a missing SQLite file are refused before Strapi's bootstrap (where it writes to the database).

tools.name: apply_edits
tools.description: Apply a plan returned by any plan_* tool, create_plugin or extract_to_plugin. Pass `planId` to apply exactly the reviewed plan, or `plan` (a full plan object) to apply one you hold. The plan is verified against disk first — if any touched file changed since it was computed, nothing is written (the changed paths are returned). ⚠️ Modifies files on disk.

planId.description: The planId from a plan_* result (preferred).

plan.description: A full, well-formed plan object (planId + fingerprints), if not using planId.

tools.name: apply_rename
tools.description: Convenience: plan + apply a rename in one call. An entity (omit `method`) or a service/controller method (pass `method`). Rewrites every call-site + route handler and renames the files/folders. ⚠️ Modifies files on disk. Prefer plan_rename_* then apply_edits when you want to review first.

ref.description: A Strapi reference: a content-type or component UID (api::article.article, shared.seo), a service / controller / policy / middleware ref (api::article.article, plugin::users-permissions.user, global::is-owner), or a route handler (api::article.article.find). `ref#method` targets one method.

newName.description: The new method name (with `method`), else the UID's new last segment (api::product.product + item → api::product.item).

method.description: Pass to rename a method; omit to rename the entity.

configSync.description: With strapi-plugin-config-sync: also update the config/sync files this refactor concerns (roles' permissions, content-manager views) to the new names. Default: true (the strapiDevkit.configSync.followRefactors setting; DEVKIT_CONFIG_SYNC_FOLLOW_REFACTORS=0 for a standalone server). Pass false when config/sync is not yours to change here (exported from another environment). The plan's warnings say which sync files it updates, or leaves with the old names.

from.description: A path inside the target project (e.g. the file you are editing). Disambiguates a multi-project workspace.

project.description: A project name (its folder) or root path. Use when you have no file path in hand.

instructions:
DevKit for Strapi knows the real UIDs, services, controllers, policies, middlewares, routes and schemas of the Strapi projects in this workspace, read statically (Strapi is not started — except by the Pro config_sync_diff/export/import tools, which load it when called).
1. Orient: list_projects (several projects → pass `from`, a path inside the one you work on, to every tool); project_info for one project in full.
2. Before writing a magic string (UID, service/controller ref, route handler, policy), call validate_reference: `unknown` comes with didYouMean; `external` means the plugin can't be verified (project_info says why). Never invent a UID.
3. Read the real shape: get_schema for fields, list_routes for routes, find_references / dependents before changing something.
4. Refactor in two steps: a plan_* tool (dry-run) → review → apply_edits with its planId; then list_broken_refs should return nothing.
5. When a project uses config-sync (project_info.configSync): config_sync_status lists its files. Prefer an export (the admin Config Sync page, `npx config-sync export`) to editing config/sync/*.json by hand: config-sync compares each file as written with the database.
6. With Pro, config-sync through the project's own Strapi: config_sync_diff gives the real diff (what a start changes included). After changing a schema, a controller or a route: config_sync_diff, then config_sync_export the entries your change caused, and commit them with the code. To change a role or a content-manager view: edit its file, config_sync_import it (the plugin then writes it back in its own form). A DevKit rename or move also updates the config/sync files it concerns, unless `configSync: false` is passed or the user turned it off (strapiDevkit.configSync.followRefactors): its warnings say which files it updated, or left with the old names. Importing them is the user's call — the local database is shared by every branch; config_sync_import loads Strapi with the new code.
Answers reflect the files on disk: what changed outside this session is re-indexed before each call (unless a project's freshness.diskTracking is 'off' — then call refresh). server_info says which tools need a Pro licence.
